name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Adopt a 3-pixel solid focus ring with a 3-pixel outer glow in the brand color for interactive elements. This ensures keyboard users see clear focus without sacrificing contrast or visual noise. The trade-off is slightly more CSS complexity, but it’s worth it for universal clarity.

name: Reader
text: Risk: The 3px ring + 3px glow creates a "halo effect" that can obscure adjacent elements, especially on dense screens. Better: Use a 2px ring with a 2px outer glow at 30% opacity—still visible but less intrusive. Settle it: Test with a 10-person keyboard-only group; if any fail to track focus or report overlap, drop the glow.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt the 2px ring with 2px outer glow at 30% opacity. It keeps focus visible without the halo risk, balancing clarity and density. Trade-off: slightly less "pop" than the 3px version, but that’s acceptable—users care more about tracking focus than intensity. This matches the reduced-motion goal by avoiding harsh edges while still working for keyboard nav.

name: Reader
text: Risk: A 2px ring with 30% opacity glow still fails WCAG 2.1 AA contrast on light brand backgrounds—measured at 3.8:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum. Better: Use a 3px ring with a 1px outer glow at 100% opacity; it meets contrast and avoids haloing. Settle it: Run a 10-person keyboard-only test with both versions—if any user loses focus visibility or reports glare, pick the 3px ring.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship a 2px solid focus ring in #0078D4 with 1px outer glow at 0s, the result must deliver sufficient contrast and visibility for keyboard navigation without introducing visual noise, and the lead developer owns ensuring this implementation is deployed and tested.
